Study_Title: BlkMaC: A Blockchain-based Multi-Agents System with LLM Communication Framework
Threat_Attacker_Model: Adversarial inter-agent eavesdropping, prompt/response tampering, intellectual property theft, and model distillation across external multi-agent communication channels (pp. 1, 3–4).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: BlkMaC hybrid encryption and blockchain-IPFS verification combining symmetric payload encryption, asymmetric key exchange, and on-chain smart contract hash verification between Controller Agent and Specialized Agents (Figures 1–2, pp. 2–4).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Controller Agent & Blockchain-IPFS Communication Middleware (Figure 1, p. 2)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Confidentiality of inter-agent task prompts/outputs, tamper-evident message integrity, and immutable on-chain auditability (pp. 3–4).
Trust_Assumptions: Controller Agent, blockchain consensus nodes, and IPFS storage layer operate honestly; participating specialized agents protect their private keys.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across 50 task rounds on 8 LLMs (Table 2, p. 6): GPT-5 achieves top score 0.91, DeepSeek-R1 0.76, and BlkMaC improves GPT-5-mini accuracy by 5% to 0.75; hybrid plaintext/ciphertext mode reduces on-chain gas cost (Figure 4, p. 6) while encryption/decryption latency is reported qualitatively as negligible (p. 1).
Exposed_Security_Function: Hybrid on-chain/off-chain encrypted inter-agent message routing and immutable smart-contract hash verification
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Lacks formal cryptographic reduction proofs and reports encryption/decryption latency only qualitatively as 'negligible' without millisecond percentile distributions (p50/p95/p99) across payload sizes.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Section 3 (pp. 2–4, Figures 1–2), and Section 4 (p. 6, Table 2 & Figure 4): "This study proposes BlkMaC, a Blockchain-based Multi-Agent System with an LLM communication framework... improves GPT-5-mini's accuracy by 5%, reaching levels comparable to larger models, while encryption/decryption latency is negligible."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: BlkMaC secures multi-agent LLM communication against tampering, IP theft, and model distillation using hybrid encryption, IPFS storage, and blockchain smart-contract verification while improving GPT-5-mini accuracy by 5% with negligible encryption latency.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Multi-agent Controller-to-Specialist communication over hybrid blockchain-IPFS channels evaluated over 50 rounds across 8 LLMs
Protected_Object: Inter-agent communication payloads, specialized agent prompts/responses, and on-chain verification hashes
Composition_Evidence: Composes encrypted Controller-to-Specialist inter-agent messaging (B2) with hybrid IPFS off-chain storage and on-chain smart-contract hash auditing (B4) (Figures 1–2, pp. 2–3).
Coding_Rationale: Dikodekan sebagai SYSTEM_PROTOTYPE pada MULTI_BOUNDARY (B2;B4) dengan status PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED (AD;UG) karena Tabel 2 dan Gambar 4 (hlm. 6) menyajikan evaluasi akurasi 50 putaran dan reduksi biaya hibrida, tetapi latensi enkripsi/dekripsi hanya diklaim 'negligible' secara kualitatif tanpa tabel distribusi waktu atau uji serangan aktif.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Blockchain Integration for Trust and Consent Management in MCP-Enabled FHIR Systems
Threat_Attacker_Model: Unauthorized clinical data access, unconsented LLM/MCP querying over HL7 FHIR patient records, stale/revoked consent bypass, and audit log tampering (pp. 1–3).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Permissioned blockchain smart-contract consent registry and cryptographic attestation ledger integrated with MCP-enabled HL7 FHIR clinical servers (Figure 1, p. 4).
Enforcement_Point_Location: MCP-FHIR Integration Gateway & Permissioned Blockchain Consent Layer (Figure 1, p. 4)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Patient consent authorization enforcement, bounded-latency consent revocation, and 100% deterministic tamper-proof audit recovery (pp. 1, 4–8).
Trust_Assumptions: Permissioned clinical blockchain consortium nodes and FHIR gateway endpoints faithfully enforce smart-contract consent state.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: On synthetic clinical FHIR cohorts, blockchain-integrated MCP adds p95 < 250 ms end-to-end latency while achieving 100% deterministic audit recovery and fast consent revocation (Abstract, p. 1; Section V, pp. 6–8).
Exposed_Security_Function: Smart-contract-gated patient consent verification, dynamic consent revocation, and immutable FHIR query audit logging
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Evaluated on synthetic clinical cohorts rather than live multi-institution WAN production traffic; does not prevent semantic inference or prompt-injection extraction from authorized FHIR fields.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1) & Section III–V (pp. 4–8, Figure 1): "On synthetic clinical cohorts, we benchmark end-to-end latency, throughput, consent-revocation latency, and audit verifiability... Results show comparable latency (p95 < 250 ms added), deterministic audit recovery (100%), and materially stronger guarantees for consent revocation and non-repudiation."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Integrating blockchain smart-contract consent management with MCP-enabled FHIR systems provides 100% deterministic audit recovery and dynamic consent revocation with p95 < 250 ms added latency.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Controlled benchmark on synthetic clinical cohorts for MCP-mediated HL7 FHIR querying with blockchain consent attestations
Protected_Object: HL7 FHIR clinical resource queries, patient consent state, and MCP invocation audit logs
Composition_Evidence: Couples pre-execution smart-contract consent verification at the MCP-FHIR tool invocation gateway (B3) with immutable on-chain audit attestation and deterministic audit recovery (B4) (Figure 1, p. 4).
Coding_Rationale: Dikodekan sebagai DEFENSIVE_MECHANISM pada MULTI_BOUNDARY (B3;B4) dengan SUPPORTED_WITHIN_SCOPE (AD;UG) karena kuantifikasi empiris p95 < 250 ms dan 100% deterministic audit recovery disajikan pada kohort klinis sintetis.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Blockchain-Assisted Time-Bound Encrypted Matching for Trustworthy Agentic-AI Edge Networking
Threat_Attacker_Model: PPT Type-I (unauthorized tester without trapdoor) and Type-II (curious tester with expired/epoch-bounded trapdoor) adversaries attempting ciphertext distinguishing or out-of-epoch risk-descriptor matching in zero-trust agentic edge networks (Section V, p. 11).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Blockchain-Assisted Time-Bound Public-Key Encryption with Equality Test (TB-PKEET) over bilinear pairing groups with epoch-bound trapdoor tokens (Figure 1, p. 2; Section IV, pp. 5–10).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Cryptographic Matching Layer & Consortium Blockchain Epoch Verifier (Figure 1, p. 2)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: OW-CCA/IND-CCA confidentiality and strict time-epoch-bounded ciphertext equality testing under the Computational Diffie-Hellman (CDH) assumption in G1 (Theorem 1, p. 11).
Trust_Assumptions: CDH problem is hard in bilinear group G1; consortium blockchain maintains synchronized time epochs and tamper-proof trapdoor authorization state.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Game-based security reduction (Theorem 1, p. 11) accompanied by prototype benchmarks showing stable 7x–11x on-/off-chain Equality Test overhead across time epochs (Abstract, p. 1; Section VI, pp. 12–16).
Exposed_Security_Function: Time-bound encrypted risk-descriptor equality testing (TB-PKEET) with formal game-based CDH reduction
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Relies on classical bilinear pairings (CDH in G1) which are broken by Shor's quantum algorithm; lattice-based post-quantum equality test/key agreement schemes are only cited in references (p. 17, refs [37, 56]).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1) & Section V (p. 11, Theorem 1): "Theorem 1: Assume the CDH assumption holds in G1... Proof: Let A1 be a PPT Type-I adversary attacking Game 1. We prove the theorem via a sequence of games."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: TB-PKEET provably guarantees confidentiality and time-bound encrypted risk-descriptor equality matching for agentic-AI edge networking under the CDH assumption in G1 (Theorem 1).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Game-based cryptographic proof (Theorem 1) for time-bound public-key encryption with equality test in agentic edge coordination
Protected_Object: Encrypted agentic edge risk descriptors and epoch-scoped equality-test trapdoors
Composition_Evidence: Composes off-chain bilinear-pairing encrypted descriptor matching between edge agents (B2) with on-chain smart-contract epoch authorization and audit logging (B4) (Figure 1, p. 2).
Coding_Rationale: Dekompisi klaim atomik (-A): memisahkan bukti reduksi kriptografis formal berbasis game (Theorem 1 pada hlm. 11 di bawah asumsi CDH pada G1) dari klaim benchmark overhead prototipe (-B).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Breaking MCP with Function Hijacking Attacks: Novel Threats for Function Calling and Agentic Models
Threat_Attacker_Model: Adversarial tool/server publisher or indirect injector who appends gradient-optimized token perturbations to MCP tool/function descriptions to hijack LLM function selection toward a target function f_target (Figure 1, p. 2; Section 4, p. 14).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Function Hijacking Attack / FHA adapting Greedy Coordinate Gradient / GCG discrete token optimization to poison MCP tool descriptions; Figure 1, p. 2; Section 4, p. 14).
Enforcement_Point_Location: LLM Function-Calling / MCP Tool Selection Context (Figure 1, p. 2)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Violates tool-selection integrity and authorization boundaries by coercing the LLM to invoke an unintended MCP tool (pp. 1–4).
Trust_Assumptions: Attacker can modify or register a candidate tool description in the MCP toolset presented to the LLM and (for white-box optimization) access open-weight model gradients.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Reaches 66.7%–100% ASR on training queries, 62.5%–81.9% ASR on held-out queries across 4 function-calling LLMs, 70%–100% single-query ASR, and 11.2%–27.6% cross-model transfer ASR; simple FHA optimization takes 1,000 epochs x 23 s/epoch (~6.4 hours) on 1 NVIDIA A100-80GB GPU (pp. 1–2; Table 10, p. 40).
Exposed_Security_Function: Gradient-based Function Hijacking Attack (FHA) formulation and multi-model MCP function-calling vulnerability benchmark
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: White-box GCG optimization requires gradient access (black-box transfer ASR drops to 11.2%–27.6%) and produces high-perplexity adversarial suffixes that can be flagged by perplexity filters or cryptographic tool-manifest pinning.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract & Section 1 (pp. 1–2, Figure 1, Table 1) and Appendix M (p. 40, Table 10): "FHA reaches 66.7-100% on sets of training queries, 62.5-81.9% ASR on held-out queries (Section 7), and 70-100% ASR under the single-query setting... FHA can be transferred to other model sizes and families (11.2-27.6% ASR)... The simple FHA attack takes a single A100-80GB GPU, 1,000 epochs, and 23 seconds per epoch."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Function Hijacking Attacks (FHA) using gradient-optimized perturbations in MCP tool descriptions achieve 62.5%–81.9% ASR on held-out queries across 4 function-calling LLMs and 11.2%–27.6% cross-model transfer ASR.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Empirical and optimization-based evaluation of MCP function-calling hijacking across 4 open-weight LLMs in TMLR (08/2026)
Protected_Object: MCP tool metadata descriptions and LLM function-calling invocation decisions
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates how adversarial perturbations embedded in MCP tool discovery descriptions (B2/B3) hijack downstream function-call execution (B3) (Figure 1, p. 2; Figure 17, p. 4).
Coding_Rationale: Studi Stream A di TMLR (08/2026, 41 hlm.) yang memformalkan objektif optimisasi FHA (hlm. 14) dan mengevaluasi ASR pada 4 model, transfer lintas-model, serta biaya komputasi A100-80GB (Tabel 10, hlm. 40); dikodekan SUPPORTED_WITHIN_SCOPE (AD;UG).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Bridging AI and software security: A comparative vulnerability assessment of LLM agent deployment paradigms
Threat_Attacker_Model: Multi-vector attacker executing 3,250 AI-centric (direct/indirect prompt injection, role confusion) and software-centric (SQLi, SSRF, privilege escalation, multi-step chained) attack scenarios across Function Calling and MCP deployments (Figures 1–2, pp. 5–6).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (5-phase comparative vulnerability assessment framework across Function Calling and MCP architectures in finance and healthcare domains; Figure 2, p. 6).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Function Calling Dispatcher & MCP Client-Server Boundary (Figures 1–2, pp. 5–6)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Quantifies comparative vulnerability exposure across prompt, protocol, and system layers (pp. 1, 15–30).
Trust_Assumptions: Evaluated agent deployments rely on baseline LLM system prompts and standard Function Calling / MCP connectors without external cryptographic capability gateways.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across 3,250 attack scenarios in finance and healthcare domains, Function Calling exhibits 73.5% overall ASR vs. 62.59% ASR for MCP (with FC showing higher system-centric vulnerability and MCP higher protocol-level exposure), while multi-stage chained attacks reach 91%–96% ASR (Abstract, p. 1; Sections 4–5, pp. 15–30).
Exposed_Security_Function: Unified 5-phase AI + software security comparative benchmark across Function Calling and MCP paradigms
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Benchmarks attack vulnerability rates across 3,250 scenarios using rule checks + LLM judges (p. 15) but does not implement or benchmark a novel cryptographic enforcement gateway.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1) & Section 3 (pp. 5–6, Figures 1–2): "We tested 3,250 attack scenarios across finance and healthcare domains... Function Calling showed higher overall attack success rates (73.5% vs 62.59% for MCP), with greater system-centric vulnerability while MCP showed greater protocol-level exposure... chained attacks achieving 91-96% success rates."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Across 3,250 attack scenarios in finance and healthcare, Function Calling shows 73.5% overall ASR versus 62.59% for MCP, while multi-step chained attacks achieve 91%–96% ASR across both deployment paradigms.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Comparative vulnerability benchmark of 3,250 attack scenarios across Function Calling and MCP in finance and healthcare
Protected_Object: Prompt instructions, MCP/FC tool invocations, and backend financial/clinical resources
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates compound vulnerability amplification where chaining prompt-level manipulation (B1) with protocol/tool invocation flaws (B3) and backend state persistence (B4) raises ASR from 62.59%–73.5% to 91%–96% (p. 1, Figure 2, p. 6).
Coding_Rationale: Studi Stream A (43 hlm.) yang menyajikan benchmark komparatif berskala besar (3.250 skenario) antara Function Calling dan MCP lintas batas B1, B3, dan B4; dikodekan EMPIRICAL_BENCHMARK dan SUPPORTED_WITHIN_SCOPE (AD;UG).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: CapAgent: Semantic Data-Flow Governance for LLM Agents in Big-Data Cognitive Computing
Threat_Attacker_Model: Prompt injection, untrusted external data taint propagation, unauthorized cross-domain data exfiltration, and confused-deputy tool calls in big-data cognitive agents (pp. 1, 5–8).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: CapAgent semantic data-flow governance middleware enforcing Denning-style security lattice labels (Lambda) and capability-scoped rules over a resource-labeled agent system S = <P, T, R, M, Lambda> (Figure 1, p. 5; Definition 1, p. 7; Table 1, p. 9).
Enforcement_Point_Location: CapAgent Semantic Data-Flow Middleware Reference Monitor (Figure 1, p. 5)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Non-bypassable monitor-side information-flow confinement and authorization independent of LLM prompt compliance (pp. 6–9).
Trust_Assumptions: Middleware reference monitor intercepts all tool calls and resource reads/writes, and resource security labels (Lambda) and policy rules are accurately compiled (p. 6).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: In reproducible synthetic trace-replay evaluation, the full CapAgent monitor reduces measured attack success from 100.00% to 0.00% while reporting false blocking rate, per-decision latency, and component ablations (Abstract, p. 1; Section 5, pp. 16–22; Conclusion, p. 25).
Exposed_Security_Function: Lattice-based semantic information-flow control (IFC) and capability-scoped tool call gating for LLM agents
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Authors explicitly disclose (Conclusion, p. 25) that evaluation is conducted on a synthetic middleware trace-replay benchmark rather than live end-to-end browser, OS, or multi-model deployments, and security is conditional on label compilation accuracy (p. 6).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Section 3 (pp. 6–9, Definition 1 & Table 1), and Section 6 (p. 25): "Definition 1 (Resource-labeled agent system). An agent system is a tuple S = <P, T, R, M, Lambda>... In this synthetic trace-replay evaluation, the full monitor reduces measured attack success from 100.00% to 0.00%... the paper establishes the monitor-side authorization semantics and a reproducible middleware replay result."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: CapAgent enforces semantic data-flow governance over resource-labeled LLM agents, reducing attack success from 100.00% to 0.00% in reproducible middleware trace-replay evaluation.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Formal resource-labeled IFC model (Def. 1) and synthetic trace-replay middleware evaluation in MDPI Big Data Cogn. Comput. (2026)
Protected_Object: Labeled enterprise data resources (R), agent memory state (M), and tool invocations (T)
Composition_Evidence: Propagates security labels from external resource ingestion and agent memory (B4) into deterministic pre-execution capability and lattice checks at the tool invocation monitor (B3) (Figure 1, p. 5; Table 1, p. 9).
Coding_Rationale: Studi M_AND_A yang memadukan model formal sistem agen berlabel (Def. 1, hlm. 7) dengan evaluasi trace-replay terukur (ASR 100,00% -> 0,00%) serta disklaimer eksplisit tentang batasan trace-replay vs. live OS/browser agent pada hlm. 25.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: CapChain: A Capability-Token Access Control Architecture with Verifiable Provenance for Multi-Agent LLM Systems
Threat_Attacker_Model: Over-privileged sub-agents, confused-deputy delegation, inter-agent contextual privacy leakage of confidential reservation prices, and provenance tampering in multi-agent LLM workflows (pp. 1–6).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: CapChain capability-token access control using HMAC-SHA256 unforgeable tokens (reduced to Bellare PRF/collision-resistance, pp. 5–6), Merkle/hash-chained verifiable provenance, and a 3-tier semantic redactor (Figure 1, p. 3; Sections 3–4, pp. 5–14).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Inter-Agent Capability Reference Monitor & Provenance Redaction Bus (Figure 1, p. 3)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Capability token unforgeability, monotonic privilege attenuation, tamper-evident hash-chained provenance, and inter-agent private-field redaction (pp. 5–14).
Trust_Assumptions: Underlying hash function satisfies PRF/collision-resistance assumptions (pp. 5–6) and all inter-agent messages traverse the CapChain reference monitor.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across 150 experimental conditions (25 MAGPIE negotiation scenarios x 3 open-source LLMs x 2 instruction modes), the Salient-tier redactor triggers on 4.67% of inter-agent messages with sub-millisecond HMAC token and hash-chain verification overhead (Abstract, p. 1; Section 5, pp. 15–24).
Exposed_Security_Function: HMAC capability-token attenuation, Merkle/hash-chained provenance logging, and tiered inter-agent PII/secret redaction
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Rule/salience-tier redaction can miss subtly paraphrased or indirect numerical hints across multi-turn negotiations.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1) & Sections 2–5 (pp. 3–24, Figure 1): "CapChain: A Capability-Token Access Control Architecture with Verifiable Provenance for Multi-Agent LLM Systems... Across 150 conditions (25 scenarios x 3 open-source models x 2 instruction modes), the Salient tier triggers the redactor for 4.67% of inter-agent messages."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: CapChain enforces unforgeable HMAC capability tokens, hash-chained provenance, and tiered semantic redaction across multi-agent LLM systems, triggering Salient-tier redaction on 4.67% of messages across 150 MAGPIE negotiation conditions.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Multi-agent capability access control, hash-chain provenance, and MAGPIE negotiation evaluation in MDPI Appl. Sci. (2026)
Protected_Object: Capability tokens, inter-agent negotiation messages, confidential private fields, and provenance hash chains
Composition_Evidence: Chains cryptographic HMAC capability token verification and salience-based message redaction across inter-agent handoffs (B2/B3) with hash-chained provenance audit logs (B4) (Figure 1, p. 3).
Coding_Rationale: Dekompisi klaim atomik (-A): menangkap arsitektur pertahanan CapChain (HMAC capability tokens + hash-chained provenance + tiered redaction) beserta reduksi kriptografis Bellare (hlm. 5–6).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: CLSOM: Closed-Loop Security Orchestration for Multi-Agent Systems with Trust Scoring, Policy Adaptation, and Runtime Evaluation
Threat_Attacker_Model: Post-authentication runtime attacks in multi-agent systems including behavioral drift, privilege escalation, unauthorized tool invocation, and staggered multi-agent collusion (Tables I–II, pp. 1–2).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: CLSOM Closed-Loop Security Orchestration combining telemetry collection, anomaly detection, bounded trust-score projection (Theorem 1, Eq. 2, p. 9), and automated policy adaptation (Tables I–II, pp. 1–2).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Closed-Loop Runtime Security Orchestrator & Policy Enforcement Layer (pp. 2–4)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Bounded trust score invariant Ti(t) in [0,1] (Theorem 1, p. 9), 79.0% runtime attack reduction, and rapid containment/isolation of compromised agents (Table XVI, p. 9).
Trust_Assumptions: Runtime telemetry pipeline is intact and attacker collusion does not simultaneously corrupt all behavioral observation windows (p. 3).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: In closed-loop runs (Table XVI, p. 9), CLSOM achieves 79.0% ± 2.1% attack reduction (vs. 61.4% Static, 71.0% RAAC, 67.3% SOAR), 12.8 ± 1.8 s time to first restriction, 112.3 ± 8 s isolation time, and 119 ms mean post-window processing latency (Abstract, p. 1; Table XVI, p. 9).
Exposed_Security_Function: Continuous multi-agent behavioral trust scoring, anomaly detection, and closed-loop privilege restriction/isolation
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Because restriction occurs after behavioral windows (12.8 s mean time to first restriction), 386 ± 31 malicious actions still complete before containment (Table XVI, p. 9), and staggered collusion resilience is acknowledged as an open proof gap (p. 3).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1) & Section V (p. 9, Theorem 1 & Table XVI): "In closed-loop runs, CLSOM reports 79% attack reduction, 12.8 s mean time to first restriction, and 119 ms mean post-window processing latency... Theorem 1. If Ti(0) in [0, 1] and the update in Eq. 2 applies... Table XVI: CLSOM Attack reduction 79.0 ± 2.1%, First restriction 12.8 ± 1.8 s, Isolation 112.3 ± 8 s."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: CLSOM achieves 79.0% ± 2.1% attack reduction, 12.8 s time to first restriction, and 119 ms post-window processing latency in closed-loop multi-agent security orchestration while guaranteeing bounded trust scores Ti(t) in [0,1] (Theorem 1).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Closed-loop runtime trust scoring and automated policy containment benchmarked against Static, RAAC, and SOAR baselines

Study_Title: Developing MCP-Based LLM Agents for Secure Autonomous Vehicle Planning
Threat_Attacker_Model: Man-in-the-middle map/sensor payload tampering and indirect prompt injection embedded in external navigation/map resources retrieved via MCP to cause autonomous vehicle collisions (Figures 1–3, pp. 6–8).

Security_Property_Guaranteed: Message authenticity/integrity of external MCP map data and prevention of prompt-injected trajectory collisions (pp. 1, 9–17).

Performance_Overhead_Reported: Without defense, poisoned MCP map data causes 100% collision ASR (30/30 trials on Gemma-3-12B-it-q8, p. 14); integrating the digital signing module and runtime validator blocks forged and prompt-injected driving trajectories with minimal latency overhead (Abstract, p. 1; Section 5, pp. 14–17).
Exposed_Security_Function: Cryptographic digital signature verification on MCP resource payloads combined with runtime trajectory prompt-injection validation
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Explicitly notes reliance on classical signature schemes ('remains secure against classical (non-quantum) attacks as of 2025', p. 7) and evaluates in simulated AV driving scenarios rather than physical vehicle hardware.

Gemma-3-12B-it-q8 30/30 100% [collision ASR before defense]."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Combining an MCP digital signing module with a runtime prompt-injection validator prevents 100% collision attacks (30/30 trials on Gemma-3-12B-it-q8) caused by tampered or poisoned external map data in autonomous vehicle planning.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: MCP-based autonomous vehicle motion planning evaluated across 30 adversarial map-poisoning scenarios
Protected_Object: External MCP map/navigation payloads and LLM autonomous driving motion plans
Composition_Evidence: Composes cryptographic digital signature verification on inbound MCP resource payloads (B4/B3) with pre-actuation runtime prompt-injection validation on generated driving plans (B3) (Figures 2–3, p. 8; p. 17).

Study_Title: Device-Native Autonomous Agents for Privacy-Preserving Negotiations

Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Multi-round offer trajectories still leak 11–15 bits of mutual information (Table VII, p. 7) and on-device execution requires up to 8 MB local state on mobile/edge hardware (p. 2).

TABLE VII: B2B Negotiation E2E Results (High-End Device): Average Success 87%, Latency 527 ms (Bulk 380 ms, Contract 520 ms, Multi-term 680 ms), Energy 4.7 J, Privacy 13 bits, Fair 0.85 (N=150 per scenario)."

Study_Title: Entitlement-Aware Authorization for MCP-Based AI Search and Chat Systems
Threat_Attacker_Model: Shared service-account credential abuse (Pattern 1, Fig. 1, p. 3), unauthorized tool invocation, missing step-up MFA on sensitive tools, and cross-region/row data leakage in MCP enterprise search and chat systems (pp. 1–3).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Entitlement-aware MCP authorization architecture combining OAuth 2.0 RFC 8693 On-Behalf-Of (OBO) token exchange, RFC 9449 DPoP proof-of-possession sender-constrained tokens, and an OPA/Rego Policy Decision Point (PDP) returning allow/MFA decisions plus row-level filter obligations (Figure 1, p. 3; Rego listing, p. 6).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Per-Tool MCP Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) & OPA/Rego Policy Decision Point (PDP) (pp. 3–6)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: End-to-end user identity propagation, step-up MFA enforcement on sensitive tools (e.g., finance.get_report), and obligation-driven row-level data filtering (e.g., region-scoped loan records, p. 6).
Trust_Assumptions: MCP server PEPs faithfully enforce PDP allow decisions and attach returned filter obligations to backend database/search queries.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Architectural analysis estimates PDP overhead is dominated by one local HTTP round-trip per tool call (~5 ms over a production service mesh), while explicitly listing empirical measurement of policy-evaluation latency as future work (Section VI, p. 6).
Exposed_Security_Function: OBO/DPoP user identity propagation and OPA/Rego PDP authorization with row-level filter obligations for MCP tools
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Provides concrete OPA/Rego policy rules and architectural patterns (pp. 2–6), but explicitly defers empirical policy-evaluation latency and attack-blocking benchmarks to future work (Section VI, item v, p. 6).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Table I (p. 2), Figure 1 (p. 3), and Section VI (p. 6): "This paper defines an entitlement-aware authorization architecture for MCP, a first-class Policy Decision Point (PDP) and per-tool Policy Enforcement Point (PEP)... overhead is dominated by one HTTP round-trip per tool call (typically < 5 ms over a service mesh in production)... Future work includes (v) empirical measurement of policy-evaluation latency."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: An entitlement-aware MCP architecture using OAuth 2.0 OBO/DPoP tokens and an OPA/Rego PDP enforces per-user tool authorization, MFA step-up, and row-level filter obligations across enterprise search and chat tools.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Reference authorization architecture and OPA/Rego policy specification for MCP enterprise search/chat systems
Protected_Object: User OBO/DPoP identity tokens, MCP tool invocations, and row-level enterprise search/database records
Composition_Evidence: Propagates authenticated user claims and MFA context (B1/B2) into per-tool PEP/PDP evaluation at MCP invocation (B3) and binds returned filter obligations to backend row-level data retrieval (B4) (p. 6).
Coding_Rationale: Studi Stream A (7 hlm.) yang menyajikan arsitektur otorisasi MCP berbasis OBO/DPoP dan aturan konkret OPA/Rego (hlm. 6), namun secara eksplisit menyatakan bahwa pengukuran empiris latensi merupakan pekerjaan masa depan (hlm. 6); dikodekan CONCEPTUAL_ARCHITECTURE dan PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED (AD;UG).

Study_Title: ETDI: Mitigating Tool Squatting and Rug Pull Attacks in Model Context Protocol (MCP) by Using OAuth-Enhanced Tool Definitions and Policy-Based Access Control
Threat_Attacker_Model: Tool Squatting (malicious MCP servers registering lookalike/conflicting tool names) and Rug Pull attacks (dynamic post-approval mutation of MCP tool definitions/schemas to inject malicious instructions) (pp. 1–4).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Enhanced Tool Definition Interface (ETDI) extending MCP tool manifests with cryptographic digital signatures, immutable version/hash pinning (storeApproval), OAuth 2.0 granular scopes, and Cedar/OPA policy-based access control (Figures 1–2, p. 2; Section IV, pp. 4–8).

Security_Property_Guaranteed: Cryptographic authenticity and integrity of MCP tool definitions, detection of post-approval Rug Pull schema mutations via hash pinning, and OAuth 2.0 scope-bounded invocation (pp. 4–9).
Trust_Assumptions: OAuth 2.0 identity providers and tool publisher signing keys are secure, and the MCP client host verifies ETDI signatures and pinned hashes before every tool call.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Discusses runtime overhead of JWT/signature validation and remote policy engine calls qualitatively, recommending local caching to reduce latency (Sections V–VI, pp. 8–9); no quantitative benchmark tables are reported.
Exposed_Security_Function: Cryptographically signed MCP tool definitions, hash-pinned approval state, and OAuth 2.0 scope-bound tool invocation
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Foundational arXiv (2506.01333v1) architectural specification with pseudocode/sequence diagrams (pp. 2–8), but lacks quantitative latency benchmarks or empirical ASR measurements.

Runtime Overhead: JWT validation and especially remote policy engine calls introduce latency."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: ETDI mitigates Tool Squatting and Rug Pull attacks in MCP through cryptographically signed tool definitions, immutable hash pinning, OAuth 2.0 scopes, and policy-based access control.

Protected_Object: MCP tool definitions, approval hashes, OAuth 2.0 scopes, and tool invocation requests

Study_Title: Evaluating Prompt Injection Risk and Guardrails in LLM-Enabled Home IoT Assistants
Threat_Attacker_Model: Four smart-home IoT attack scenarios (Table II, p. 5): direct prompt injection requesting household power shutdown (A1), guest-to-owner role confusion (A2), indirect prompt injection via poisoned thermostat manual (A3), and authenticated under-privileged escalation (A4).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Layered smart-home IoT guardrail pipeline combining input sanitization, RAG source filtering, role-aware context tagging, and deterministic pre-actuation policy gating (Figure 1 & Table I, p. 4; Table II, p. 5).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Layered IoT Assistant Pipeline & Pre-Actuation Policy Gate (Figure 1, p. 4)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Lowers Attack Success Rate (ASR) to 0.00 across scenarios A1–A4 when deterministic pre-actuation policy gating is enabled (pp. 5–6).
Trust_Assumptions: Deterministic policy gate sits inline before physical smart-home IoT device actuation and caller authentication role (owner vs. guest) is bound outside the LLM prompt.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across incremental guardrail configurations on scenarios A1–A4 (Tables I–II, pp. 4–6): prompt-level guardrails alone leave residual vulnerability because the LLM fails to reliably follow role labels (p. 4), whereas adding deterministic pre-actuation policy gating reduces ASR to 0.00 (p. 6).
Exposed_Security_Function: Multi-layer input/RAG sanitization and deterministic role-based policy gating for LLM-enabled smart-home IoT assistants
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Evaluated on a small simulated smart-home scenario set (A1–A4 in Table II, p. 5) rather than large-scale physical IoT testbeds.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Section III–IV (pp. 4–6, Figure 1, Tables I–II): "Table II Simulation Scenario Set Used in the Reported Run (A1–A4)... prompt-only defenses fail when the model does not recall or follow a role label... adding deterministic policy gating lowered ASR to 0.00, illustrating the necessity of enforcement outside the LLM."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: In LLM-enabled smart-home IoT assistants, prompt-level role labels alone fail to block direct and indirect prompt injections (A1–A4), whereas deterministic pre-actuation policy gating lowers ASR to 0.00.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Ablation benchmark across layered guardrails on 4 smart-home IoT attack archetypes (A1–A4)
Protected_Object: Smart-home IoT device actuation commands, user role permissions, and RAG device manuals
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates through incremental ablation (Table I, pp. 4–6) that input/prompt guardrails (B1) and RAG sanitization (B4) must be composed with deterministic pre-execution policy gating at the device actuation boundary (B3) to reach 0.00 ASR.
Coding_Rationale: Studi Stream A (6 hlm.) yang membuktikan secara empiris melalui ablasi bertahap bahwa pelabelan peran di dalam prompt gagal, dan hanya kombinasi dengan policy gating deterministik pra-eksekusi yang menurunkan ASR ke 0,00 (hlm. 5–6).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Execution-Aware Stage-Wise Evaluation Framework for Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM-Based Email Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) embedded in untrusted incoming emails attempting to hijack LLM-based email agents into executing unauthorized API calls (e.g., SEND_EMAIL data exfiltration; Figure 1, p. 3; p. 19).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: EASE (Execution-Aware Stage-Wise Evaluation) framework decomposing IPI evaluation into fine-grained pre-execution, argument-generation, and verified post-execution outcome stages across 97 tasks and 629 security cases (Figure 1, p. 3; Table 1, p. 5).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Stage-Wise Tool Invocation & Post-Execution Outcome Verifier in LLM Email Agents (pp. 3–6)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Eliminates proxy-judge ASR overestimation by verifying actual tool execution outcomes across multi-stage email agent pipelines (pp. 1–6).
Trust_Assumptions: Benchmark harness inspects both intermediate LLM tool-call generations and actual sandboxed email API execution state.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across LLM email agents and 629 security test cases: demonstrates that conventional proxy-judged evaluation misclassifies 13.9% of proxy-judged attack successes, which are actually execution failures when verified at the runtime execution stage (Abstract, p. 1; Section I, p. 2).
Exposed_Security_Function: Execution-aware stage-wise IPI vulnerability evaluation (EASE) quantifying proxy-judge vs. true execution ASR
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Focuses on stage-wise evaluation methodology for email agents rather than proposing a cryptographic runtime defense.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract & Section I (pp. 1–2) and Table 1 (p. 5): "13.9% of proxy-judged successes are actually failures when the execution outcome is verified... conventional evaluation overestimates the true ASR by misclassifying 13.9% of proxy-judged cases."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: The Execution-Aware Stage-Wise Evaluation (EASE) framework reveals that 13.9% of proxy-judged Indirect Prompt Injection successes in LLM email agents are actually failures when runtime tool execution outcomes are verified.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Stage-wise empirical IPI evaluation across LLM-based email agents (20 pp.)
Protected_Object: Email agent tool invocations (SEND_EMAIL, READ_EMAIL) and user inbox data
Composition_Evidence: Traces how untrusted email ingestion (B4/B1) propagates through reasoning into formatted API call generation (B3) and actual environment state change (B4), revealing a 13.9% gap between proxy generation and true execution (pp. 1–5).
Coding_Rationale: Studi Stream A (20 hlm.) yang memperkenalkan kerangka kerja evaluasi bertahap EASE dan membuktikan bahwa 13,9% keberhasilan serangan yang dinilai oleh proxy sebenarnya gagal saat hasil eksekusi API diverifikasi (hlm. 1–2).

Study_Title: Execution-bound advisory automation for agentic AI: a reproducible AIBOM-driven CSAF-VEX framework
Threat_Attacker_Model: Supply-chain vulnerabilities, unverified AI Bill of Materials (AIBOM) components, and false-positive/ungrounded CVE exploitability claims across foundation models, prompt templates, MCP tool connectors, and containers (pp. 1–4).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Execution-bound advisory automation binding AIBOM component inventories and runtime execution telemetry to cryptographically signed, reproducible CSAF/VEX (Vulnerability-Exploitability eXchange) advisories (Figure 1, pp. 3–4; Table 1, p. 6).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Runtime Telemetry Collector & AIBOM/VEX Advisory Verification Pipeline (Figure 1, p. 3)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Verifiable execution-bound exploitability attestation, reducing static SBOM-CVE false positives by up to 42% (Abstract, p. 1).
Trust_Assumptions: Containerized runtime telemetry and AIBOM manifest extractors accurately record active code/tool execution paths.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Achieves an F1-score of 0.93 (precision 0.96, recall 0.92), reduces false positives by up to 42% relative to static SBOM-CVE matching without runtime validation, and alters exploitability outcomes in 31% of AI-specific artefact cases through AIBOM enrichment (Abstract, p. 1; Sections 3–4, pp. 6–15).
Exposed_Security_Function: Reproducible AIBOM-driven runtime exploitability verification and automated VEX/CSAF advisory generation
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Authors explicitly caution (Section 1.1, p. 2) against extrapolating controlled benchmark results to definitive claims of real-world zero-day exploitability prediction accuracy.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Section 1.1 (p. 2), Figure 1 (p. 3), and Section 4 (p. 13): "achieves an F1-score of 0.93 (precision 0.96, recall 0.92), reduces false positives by up to 42% relative to static SBOM–CVE matching without runtime validation, and alters exploitability outcomes in 31% of AI-specific artefact cases through AIBOM enrichment."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Execution-bound AIBOM advisory automation achieves 0.93 F1-score (0.96 precision, 0.92 recall), reduces false positives by up to 42% over static SBOM-CVE matching, and alters exploitability status in 31% of AI-specific artefact cases.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Reproducible AIBOM + runtime execution advisory automation evaluated in Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence (2026)
Protected_Object: AIBOM component manifests, tool connectors, container execution traces, and VEX/CSAF security advisories
Composition_Evidence: Binds live tool-connector and container execution traces (B3) to AIBOM dependency graphs and reproducible VEX/CSAF audit advisories (B4) (Figure 1, p. 3; p. 13).
Coding_Rationale: Artikel Frontiers in AI (Radanliev et al., 2026, 21 hlm.) yang menyajikan metrik presisi 0,96, recall 0,92, F1 0,93, dan reduksi false positive 42% untuk otomasi advisory berbasis AIBOM.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Taxonomy of MCP attack surfaces and countermeasures across five workflow stages (citing ETDI OAuth/signed tool definitions and demonstrating a lightweight output auditing proof-of-concept; Figures 3–5, pp. 4–7).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Across the 5 Stages of the MCP Client-Server Workflow (Figures 2–4, pp. 3–6)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Systematizes attack vectors and stage-wise defense requirements across function calling and MCP ecosystems (pp. 3–10).
Trust_Assumptions: Open MCP server registries (>5,000 community servers cited on p. 2) contain untrusted third-party tool providers.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Architectural survey and vulnerability taxonomy (ZTE Communications, Sept 2025) with a qualitative case study / lightweight output-auditing PoC (Figure 5, p. 7); no quantitative benchmark tables are reported.
Exposed_Security_Function: Five-stage MCP attack surface taxonomy and defense mapping (registration, discovery, planning, invocation, output auditing)
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Architectural review and qualitative PoC illustration (Figure 5, p. 7) without large-scale empirical ASR or latency measurements.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Section 2–4 (pp. 2–9, Figures 2–5): "Fig. 3 summarizes the main attack surfaces identified across the five stages of the Model Context Protocol workflow... Fig. 4. Defense strategies across the MCP workflow stages... we also implement a lightweight output auditing mechanism as a proof-of-concept (p. 7)."

Study_Title: Future-Proofing Identity Security for Agentic AI Systems: Design, Implementation, and Evaluation of an Identity Fabric
Threat_Attacker_Model: Five agentic identity failure classes (Table X, p. 6): credential theft, agent impersonation, scope escalation across multi-hop delegation, intent drift, and untrusted agent discovery.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Six composable identity primitives including Ephemeral Attested Agent Identity (EAAI, 300 s TTL, Kubernetes SA binding), Intent-Bound Delegation Tokens (IBDT, originator intent hash + monotonic scope narrowing S_child subseteq S_parent), DPoP proof-of-possession, and Decentralized Agent Identity Registry (DAIR) (Tables I–II, p. 2; Table X, p. 6).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Agent Identity Issuance Plane & Inter-Agent / Tool Delegation Verifier (Table X, p. 6)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: 100% delegation scope narrowing fidelity (20/20 tests), originator intent-hash preservation, non-renewable 300 s ephemeral credentials, and 63 ms revocation propagation (p. 1; Table X, p. 6).
Trust_Assumptions: Kubernetes workload attestation (SA binding) and cryptographic hash/signature primitives are uncompromised.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Achieves 100% delegation fidelity (20/20 narrowing tests), sub-25 ms mean latency for credential issuance and delegation, 52 ms cold-path / 11 ms warm-path authentication, 63 ms credential revocation, and 203 ms total identity overhead on a multi-agent workflow with Claude Sonnet (representing only 2.6% of total LLM inference latency; Abstract, p. 1; Table X, p. 6).
Exposed_Security_Function: Ephemeral Attested Agent Identity (EAAI) and Intent-Bound Delegation Tokens (IBDT) with monotonic scope narrowing
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Intent-hash binding preserves cryptographic integrity of the original intent text but relies on policy/semantic checks to verify whether dynamically generated sub-tasks match that intent.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1) & Section V (p. 6, Table X): "achieved 100% delegation fidelity (20/20 narrowing tests), sub-25 ms mean latency for credential issuance and delegation, and authentication with 52 ms cold-path and 11 ms warm-path... with Claude Sonnet, total identity overhead was 203 ms, representing 2.6% of inference latency... Table X: EAAI 300 s TTL, revocation in 63 ms."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Composable EAAI and IBDT primitives achieve 100% monotonic delegation fidelity (20/20), sub-25 ms issuance/delegation latency, 63 ms revocation, and 203 ms total identity overhead (2.6% of Claude Sonnet inference latency).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Design, implementation, and latency/security evaluation of 6 agentic IAM primitives across multi-hop delegation workflows
Protected_Object: Ephemeral agent identities (EAAI, 300s TTL), Intent-Bound Delegation Tokens (IBDT), and originator intent hashes
Composition_Evidence: Cryptographically binds originator user intent hash (B1) into monotonically narrowed IBDT tokens across multi-hop agent delegations (B2) and tool invocations (B3) with 63 ms revocation and auditability (B4) (Table X, p. 6).
Coding_Rationale: Studi M_AND_A yang sangat kuat secara teknis: merinci 6 primitif identitas (EAAI, IBDT, DAIR, dll.) dan melaporkan angka latensi terukur yang lengkap (sub-25 ms issuance, 52/11 ms cold/warm auth, 63 ms revocation, 203 ms / 2,6% total overhead dengan Claude Sonnet).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Governance-as-Code: Managing Agentic AI with a Distributed Dual Proxy Gateway
Threat_Attacker_Model: Ungoverned agentic tool/microservice invocations, policy bypass at edge nodes, and tampered inter-service requests/responses (pp. 122–126 / PDF pp. 1–5).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Governance-as-Code distributed dual-proxy gateway architecture combining lightweight WebAssembly (Wasm) edge proxies, heavyweight core proxies, and cryptographic request/response signing across invoked microservices (Figures 1–4, pp. 5–7 / Procedia CS pp. 126–129).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Distributed Dual Proxy Gateway (Lightweight Wasm Edge Proxy + Heavyweight Core Proxy; pp. 3–5)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Sandbox-isolated Wasm policy execution at the edge, global Governance-as-Code enforcement, and cryptographic request/response non-repudiation across microservices (pp. 1, 5–6).
Trust_Assumptions: Wasm runtime sandbox is memory-safe and microservice signing keys are securely provisioned.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Micro-benchmarks show Wasm-mediated validation adds <= 20 ns overhead for simple CPU-bound calls (93 ns native host vs. 115 ns Wasm, Figures 1–2, p. 5) and ~120 ns when crossing host-Wasm boundaries; for 100x100 matrix workloads, median execution time is 3.1 ms native vs. nearly identical in Wasm (Figures 3–4, pp. 5–7).
Exposed_Security_Function: Wasm-sandboxed Governance-as-Code dual-proxy policy validation and microservice request/response signing
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Micro-benchmarks evaluate synthetic CPU/matrix workloads in native vs. Wasm (Figures 1–4, pp. 5–7) rather than end-to-end adversarial prompt injection or cryptographic signing throughput under WAN load.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1 / p. 122) & Section 4 (pp. 5–7 / pp. 126–128, Figures 1–4): "Micro-benchmarks show that Wasm-mediated validation adds <= 20 ns overhead for CPU-bound tasks and ~120 ns when crossing boundaries... median execution time within the host program is 93 ns, increasing to 115 ns when calling the function in the Wasm module... To establish proof, each invoked microservice cryptographically signs the request/response."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: A distributed dual-proxy Governance-as-Code gateway using WebAssembly (Wasm) edge modules and cryptographic microservice signing adds <= 20 ns CPU validation overhead (93 ns native vs. 115 ns Wasm) and ~120 ns boundary-crossing overhead.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Dual-proxy Governance-as-Code architecture and Wasm vs. native micro-benchmarks in Procedia Computer Science 272 (2025)
Protected_Object: Edge/core Governance-as-Code policy modules and signed microservice requests/responses
Composition_Evidence: Coordinates lightweight Wasm edge proxy guardrails (B2/B3) with heavyweight core proxy policy orchestration and cryptographically signed microservice request/response logs (B4) (pp. 3–6).
Coding_Rationale: Artikel Procedia Computer Science 272 (2025, hlm. 122–130) yang menyajikan arsitektur dual-proxy Wasm + penandatanganan kriptografis microservice dengan micro-benchmark terukur (93 ns native vs 115 ns Wasm, <=20 ns overhead).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Governed Agentic Cloud Data Pipelines with MCP Gateways
Threat_Attacker_Model: Schema drift, injected policy/security violations, and unvalidated tool arguments in autonomous agentic cloud data and ML pipelines (pp. 1–2).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Governed MCP Gateway architecture combining four incremental enforcement layers: Schema Validation, Compatibility Management, Policy Enforcement, and Telemetry/Auditing (Figure 1, p. 3; Table III, p. 5).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Governed MCP Gateway between Orchestration Agents and Cloud Data/ML Pipelines (Figure 1, p. 3)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Blocks > 96% of injected schema, policy, and security violations while improving pipeline execution success to 99.7% and reducing MTTR by 58.3% (Abstract, p. 1; Table III, p. 5).
Trust_Assumptions: All agentic data-pipeline tool invocations traverse the governed MCP gateway and schema/policy registries are intact.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Ablation across trials (Table III & Figure 3, p. 5) shows progressive gains from Schema Validation Only (94.2% success, 9.3 s MTTR, 1.2% overhead), +Compatibility Management (96.4%, 7.1 s, 2.8%), +Policy Enforcement (98.3%, 5.6 s, 4.2%), to Full Gateway with Telemetry & Auditing (99.7% success, 4.75 s MTTR / 58.3% reduction, >96% violation blocking, and < 6.2% p95 end-to-end latency overhead).
Exposed_Security_Function: Four-layer MCP gateway governance (schema validation, compatibility checks, policy enforcement, and telemetry auditing)
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Up to 4% of complex semantic policy/schema violations still bypass static gateway rules (<96% blocked), and no cryptographic token/signature proof is presented.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1) & Section V (p. 5, Table III & Figure 3): "improves pipeline execution success rate by up to 7.6% [to 99.7%], reduces mean time to recovery by 58.3% [to 4.75 s], blocks over 96% of injected schema, policy, and security violations, and introduces less than 6.2% p95 end-to-end latency overhead."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Governed MCP gateways for agentic cloud data pipelines block over 96% of injected schema, policy, and security violations, achieve 99.7% execution success, reduce MTTR by 58.3% (to 4.75 s), and add < 6.2% p95 latency overhead.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Controlled ablation benchmark across public cloud data/ML pipeline workloads (Table I & Table III)
Protected_Object: Cloud data pipeline schemas, MCP tool invocations, and execution audit logs
Composition_Evidence: Ablation in Table III (p. 5) quantifies the additive composition of pre-execution schema, compatibility, and policy enforcement (B3) with post-execution telemetry and auditing (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Studi M_AND_A yang menyajikan hasil ablasi kuantitatif 4 lapis pada Tabel III (hlm. 5): akurasi sukses 99,7%, MTTR 4,75 detik (-58,3%), pemblokiran >96% pelanggaran, dan p95 overhead <6,2%.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Guarding the Gateway: Securing MCP-Mediated RAG Pipelines Against Injection with the Guru Framework
Threat_Attacker_Model: Indirect prompt injection, RAG knowledge poisoning, context-boundary manipulation, and unauthorized cross-domain tool escalation in MCP-mediated enterprise RAG pipelines (Section III, pp. 2–3).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Guru five-layer defense-in-depth retrieval validation architecture defined by algebraic scoring formulas (Eqs. 1–19, pp. 2–5): cosine semantic similarity (Si), normalized Shannon entropy anomaly (Ai), context boundary compliance (Bi), source trust (Ts), intent consistency (Ic), privilege ratio (Pl), graph propagation risk (Rn), sanitization confidence (Cs), and adaptive threshold (theta_t). Contains no cryptographic chunk hashing.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Five-Layer Guru Retrieval Security & Control Layer between MCP Sources and LLM Context (Figure 1, p. 2)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Reports empirical reduction in context contamination and injection leakage (CIR 96.8%, IRI 95.9%, SIS 96.1% in Table II; RTS 0.95, ATRE 0.94 in Table III, p. 5) without formal security proofs.
Trust_Assumptions: Embedding model, entropy/trust scoring thresholds, and five-layer Guru validation pipeline operate within a trusted host boundary.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Reports summary defense metrics in Table II (CIR 96.8%, IRI 95.9%, SIS 96.1%) and Table III (RTS 0.95, ATRE 0.94) on p. 5, but omits dataset size, number of attacks, LLM models, hardware environment, and latency/throughput overhead.
Exposed_Security_Function: Five-layer retrieval validation (entropy/semantic anomaly scoring, boundary compliance, source trust ranking, graph interaction monitoring, and adaptive sanitization)
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Equations 1–19 are heuristic weighted algebraic definitions rather than formal security proofs; Tables II–III report high percentages (CIR 96.8%, IRI 95.9%) without specifying benchmark dataset size, LLM backbones, hardware, or millisecond latency overhead; quantum-resistant trust management is mentioned only in one sentence of Future Work (p. 6).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Sections III–VI (pp. 2–6, Equations 1–19, Tables II–III): "This study presents the Guru Framework, a five-layer defense-in-depth architecture designed to protect MCP-enabled RAG systems... Table II: Guru Framework (Proposed) CIR 96.8%, IRI 95.9%, SIS 96.1%; Table III: RTS 0.95, ATRE 0.94... Future directions include developing quantum-resistant trust management (p. 6)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: The five-layer Guru Framework secures MCP-mediated RAG pipelines against prompt injection and context poisoning, reporting 96.8% Context Integrity Rate (CIR), 95.9% Injection Resistance Index (IRI), and 96.1% Semantic Integrity Score (SIS).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Conceptual architecture and algebraic scoring model (Eqs. 1–19) with summary tables lacking experimental workload specifications
Protected_Object: Retrieved RAG chunks, MCP context envelopes, and downstream tool/agent interactions
Composition_Evidence: Chains five sequential filtering layers across external RAG/MCP chunk ingestion (B4), context assembly/sanitization (B1), and graph-monitored tool/agent interaction (B3) (Figure 1, p. 2; Eqs. 1–19).
Coding_Rationale: Audit baris pilot EXTRACTED (CLM-0006): mempertahankan koreksi audit v1.2 (CONCEPTUAL_ARCHITECTURE, PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, AD;UG, STAGE_1_SUGGESTED_MIGRATION untuk 1 kalimat future work di hlm. 6) serta menyempurnakan Artifact_Protection_Lifetime menjadi EPHEMERAL_SESSION dan Exposed_Security_Function secara presisi.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Hierarchical Approaches for Development of an MCP Security Framework
Threat_Attacker_Model: Layered MCP ecosystem threats motivated by real-world supply-chain/backdoor incidents (such as the September 2025 postmark-mcp email exfiltration incident, p. 1), including tool poisoning, unauthorized access, and protocol manipulation.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Hierarchical MCP Security Framework organizing asset identification, lifecycle definition, threat analysis, and defense prioritization (referencing TLS/DNSSEC RFC 4033–4035 cryptographic integrity standards, p. 12) across MCP Host, Client, Server, and External Resource layers (Figures 1–2, p. 3; Tables 6, 8, 11, pp. 9–11).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Hierarchical MCP Host, Client, Server, and Transport Layers (Figure 2, p. 3)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Provides a structured analytical threat-modeling and defense-prioritization taxonomy aligned with NIST CSF / ISO 27001 across layered MCP ecosystems (Tables 8–11, pp. 10–12).
Trust_Assumptions: Enterprise security architects apply the hierarchical investigation and defense mapping across MCP deployment lifecycles.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Analytical framework and hierarchical threat/defense mapping (Tables 1–11, pp. 3–15); authors explicitly state (Section VI-A, p. 16) that the paper offers an analytical structuring model rather than an empirical runtime benchmark.
Exposed_Security_Function: Hierarchical MCP asset/lifecycle threat modeling and defense prioritization framework
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Authors explicitly note (p. 16) that the framework provides analytical investigation guidance and defense mapping without empirical attack-blocking or latency measurements.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Figure 2 (p. 3), Tables 6, 8, 11 (pp. 9–11), and Section VI (p. 16): "threats exploiting MCP vulnerabilities materialized through the postmark-mcp incident in September 2025... its contribution lies in offering a flexible investigation-guidance and analytical structuring model that supports systematic threat analysis and defense prioritization within layered MCP ecosystems."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: A hierarchical MCP security framework structures asset identification, lifecycle threat analysis, and defense prioritization across MCP Host, Client, and Server layers following incidents like postmark-mcp.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Hierarchical threat and defense mapping framework for MCP ecosystems (Korea University, 17 pp.)
Protected_Object: MCP Host, MCP Client, MCP Server tools, and external API resources across lifecycle stages
Composition_Evidence: Maps threat propagation and defense controls hierarchically across user prompt ingestion (B1), client-server discovery (B2), tool execution (B3), and external resource/audit flows (B4) (Figure 2, p. 3; Tables 6–11, pp. 9–11).
Coding_Rationale: Studi Stream A (17 hlm.) yang menyusun kerangka kerja analitis berlapis untuk ancaman dan pertahanan MCP (termasuk analisis insiden postmark-mcp September 2025) dengan pernyataan eksplisit di hlm. 16 bahwa evaluasi bersifat analitis/konseptual; dikodekan CONCEPTUAL_ARCHITECTURE dan PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED (AD;UG).

Study_Title: Identity and Access Management for Agentic AI: A Zero-Trust Security Framework
Threat_Attacker_Model: Four agentic IAM threat classes (Table I, p. 2): token replay/hijacking, privilege escalation across sub-agent delegation, behavioral drift/prompt injection, and audit evasion.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: ZT-AgentIAM Zero-Trust security framework combining short-lived cryptographic identity tokens, fine-grained policy engine (< 1 ms for up to 500 rules, p. 3), continuous behavioral attestation (threshold tau), and tamper-evident audit logging (Tables I–IV, pp. 2–4; Figure 2, p. 4).
Enforcement_Point_Location: ZT-AgentIAM Zero-Trust Gateway (Auth + Policy Engine + Behavioral Attestation + Audit Logger; Figure 2, p. 4)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: High multi-category attack detection rate compared to baseline static IAM with bounded 15.1 ms mean full-pipeline latency overhead (Table II & Figure 2, pp. 3–4).
Trust_Assumptions: ZT-AgentIAM gateway mediates all agent API/tool calls and behavioral attestation baselines are calibrated.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Full-pipeline mean latency overhead is 15.1 ms (p99 29.4 ms), decomposed in Figure 2 (p. 4) into Identity Verification, Policy Evaluation (< 1 ms for <= 500 rules, p. 3), Behavioral Attestation (8.3 ms mean / 14.7 ms p99), and Audit Logging (0.9 ms mean / 2.4 ms p99), with threshold sensitivity trade-offs reported in Table IV (p. 4).
Exposed_Security_Function: Zero-trust agent authentication, sub-millisecond policy evaluation, behavioral attestation, and audit logging (ZT-AgentIAM)
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Behavioral attestation introduces false-positive vs. detection trade-offs across threshold settings (Table IV, p. 4) and accounts for over half (8.3 ms / 15.1 ms) of total pipeline latency.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1) & Section IV (pp. 3–4, Tables II–IV & Figure 2): "detects attacks across all four threat categories with a full-pipeline latency overhead of 15.1 ms... Policy evaluation runs in under 1 ms for sets of up to 500 rules... Figure 2: Behavioral Attestation 8.3 ms mean (14.7 ms p99), Audit Logging 0.9 ms mean (2.4 ms p99), Full Pipeline Total 15.1 ms mean (29.4 ms p99)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: ZT-AgentIAM enforces zero-trust identity verification, policy evaluation (<1 ms), behavioral attestation (8.3 ms), and audit logging (0.9 ms) across four agentic threat classes with 15.1 ms mean (29.4 ms p99) full-pipeline latency overhead.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Zero-trust IAM prototype and per-component latency/detection benchmark for agentic AI systems (5 pp.)
Protected_Object: Short-lived agent identity tokens, API/tool invocations, behavioral attestation profiles, and audit logs
Composition_Evidence: Chains per-request identity and delegation policy checks (B2/B3) with synchronous behavioral attestation (8.3 ms at B3) and audit logging (0.9 ms at B4) totaling 15.1 ms mean overhead (Figure 2, p. 4).
Coding_Rationale: Studi M_AND_A yang menyajikan rincian latensi per-komponen yang sangat jelas (Gambar 2, hlm. 4: total mean 15,1 ms, p99 29,4 ms) serta analisis sensitivitas ambang batas (Tabel IV, hlm. 4).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Identity and Access Management for AI Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Treating autonomous reasoning/delegating AI agents as human users, shared service accounts, or static stateless workloads, leading to unattributed actions, over-privileged delegation, and broken audit trails (pp. 1–5).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Reference architecture treating AI agents as first-class identity principals governed across four fundamentals via an identity gateway interposed on the agent-to-tool boundary, integrating SCIM 2.0 lifecycle provisioning, OAuth 2.0/OIDC delegation, IETF WIMSE Workload Identity Tokens + Workload Proof-of-Possession, and W3C DIDs/VCs for cross-organizational trust (Figures 1–2, pp. 3, 6; Sections 6–7, pp. 6–9).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Identity Gateway interposed on the Agent-to-Tool and Inter-Agent Boundaries (Figures 1–2, pp. 3, 6)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Unique verifiable agent identity bound to an accountable owner, least-privilege delegation scoping, and non-repudiable per-agent audit trails (pp. 1–9).
Trust_Assumptions: Enterprise IAM control plane (SCIM 2.0, OAuth/WIMSE issuers, and DID/VC trust registries) is properly governed.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Conceptual reference architecture and standards synthesis (SCIM 2.0, WIMSE, OAuth 2.0, DIDs/VCs across 10 pages); no empirical latency or attack-rate benchmarks are reported.
Exposed_Security_Function: First-class AI agent identity lifecycle management (SCIM 2.0), WIMSE workload proof tokens, and identity-gateway policy enforcement
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Conceptual architectural position paper (10 pp.) that explicitly notes unresolved governance challenges around cross-organizational DID/VC trust registries and prompt revocation of short-lived credentials (Section 8, p. 9).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Figures 1–2 (pp. 3, 6), and Sections 6–8 (pp. 6–9): "This paper argues that agents must instead be treated as first-class identity principals, each carrying a unique, verifiable identity bound to an accountable owner... WIMSE building blocks are a promising complement: a WIMSE Identity Token with a Workload Proof... SCIM 2.0 supplies the administration layer."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Treating AI agents as first-class identity principals via an identity gateway integrating SCIM 2.0, OAuth/WIMSE workload proof tokens, and DIDs/VCs resolves shared-account attribution and delegation gaps.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Reference architecture and standards mapping (SCIM 2.0, WIMSE, DIDs/VCs) for AI agent IAM (10 pp.)
Protected_Object: First-class AI agent identities, WIMSE workload proof tokens, delegated permissions, and audit trails
Composition_Evidence: Bridges human-to-agent delegation (B1), inter-agent WIMSE/DID token exchange (B2), identity-gateway-mediated tool execution (B3), and per-agent accountable audit trails (B4) (Figures 1–2, pp. 3, 6).
Coding_Rationale: Makalah arsitektur referensi Stream M (10 hlm.) yang memetakan SCIM 2.0, WIMSE, dan DID/VC pada Identity Gateway tanpa eksperimen kuantitatif; dikodekan CONCEPTUAL_ARCHITECTURE dan PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED (AD;UG).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Improving Authenticity of x402 Payment Protocol through verification of Agent's Intention with Zero-knowledge Proof
Threat_Attacker_Model: Non-deterministic or hijacked AI agents autonomously invoking paid external APIs/services via the HTTP 402 (x402) stablecoin payment protocol outside the user's intended task scope (pp. 1–2).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Intent-verified x402 payment protocol combining polynomial embedding cosine similarity (cos theta_Q,R = F(x), Eq. 5, p. 4), hash commitments to each step in the agent's Chain-of-Thought (CoT) bound to a Unique Task ID, and a Zero-Knowledge Proof (ZKP) verifying that the paid API request aligns with the user's assigned task intention before stablecoin settlement (Figures 1–2, pp. 2–3; Figure on p. 5).
Enforcement_Point_Location: x402 Resource Server / Facilitator ZKP Intention Verifier & Blockchain Settlement Layer (pp. 3–5)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Cryptographic verification that an x402-paid external API call corresponds to the user's committed task intention and Chain-of-Thought without exposing private user task secrets (pp. 1, 3–5).
Trust_Assumptions: User task commitment and secret are honestly initialized and ZKP verification circuit at the x402 resource server/facilitator is sound.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Demonstrates qualitative prompt/outcome walkthroughs (Tables 1–2, p. 4) and the 15-step x402 + ZKP + blockchain payment sequence (p. 5), but does not report quantitative ZKP proving/verification millisecond latencies or gas costs.
Exposed_Security_Function: Zero-Knowledge Proof (ZKP) verification of agent Chain-of-Thought and task-intent alignment for HTTP 402 (x402) stablecoin payments
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Presents the mathematical formulation (Eqs. 1–5, p. 4) and 2 qualitative prompt examples (Tables 1–2, p. 4), but omits ZKP circuit proving time, verification latency, and adversarial adaptive evasion benchmarks.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1) & Sections III–IV (pp. 3–5, Eq. 5, Tables 1–2): "x402 lacks the capability of verifying an agent's intention while accessing an external resource... we use a zero-knowledge proof to verify an agent's intention that verifies the commitment to each step in the chain of thought and cosine similarity cos theta_Q,R = F(x) (Eq. 5)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Integrating Zero-Knowledge Proofs of Chain-of-Thought commitment and polynomial cosine similarity into the x402 payment protocol prevents AI agents from paying for out-of-scope external API calls.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Protocol formulation and qualitative PoC walkthrough (Tables 1–2) for ZKP intent verification in x402 agent payments (University of Galway, 6 pp.)
Protected_Object: x402 stablecoin payment payloads, user task-intent secrets, and Chain-of-Thought step commitments
Composition_Evidence: Binds user task-description commitments and CoT steps (B1) to ZKP-gated HTTP 402 external tool invocation (B3) and blockchain stablecoin settlement (B4) (p. 5).
Coding_Rationale: Studi Stream M (6 hlm.) yang merumuskan verifikasi niat agen berbasis ZKP dan kemiripan kosinus polinomial (Persamaan 5, hlm. 4) pada protokol pembayaran x402 dengan 2 contoh kualitatif (Tabel 1–2, hlm. 4) tanpa tabel latensi ZKP; dikodekan PROOF_OF_CONCEPT dan PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED (AD;UG).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: In-Mig: Geographically Dispersed Agentic LLMs for Privacy-Preserving Artificial Intelligence
Threat_Attacker_Model: Cross-institutional raw data leakage when sensitive medical/legal records are centralized for LLM reasoning, as well as malicious/unauthorized mobile agent migration across organizational venues (pp. 1–6).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: In-Mig mobile-agent architecture combining JADE agent mobility, cryptographic admission/verification, containerized local Ollama runtimes for in-situ reasoning, and policy-gated sanitization/redaction of exported cross-venue summaries (Figure 3, p. 6; Tables 1–2, pp. 10–11).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Venue Admission Gate, Sandboxed Local Ollama Runtime, and Outbound Summary Redaction Filter (Figure 3, p. 6)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Raw institutional data never leaves its origin venue; only policy-sanitized summaries migrate across venues while maintaining 92% reasoning similarity to centralized GPT-4 baselines (pp. 1, 6–11).
Trust_Assumptions: Each participating institutional venue enforces container sandboxing and outbound summary redaction policies honestly.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across 4 organizational venues in legal and medical domains (Table 1 & Figure 4, pp. 9–10; Table 2, p. 11): per-venue LLM inference averages 5.1 s and memory update 1.1 s (totaling ~6.2 s per venue), achieving 92% final answer similarity to a centralized GPT-4 oracle while keeping raw data local.
Exposed_Security_Function: In-situ mobile-agent LLM reasoning (JADE + containerized Ollama) with venue admission verification and cross-venue summary redaction
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Evaluated on a synthetic multi-venue medical/legal benchmark (p. 14); sequential mobile-agent migration adds ~6.2 s latency per hop and remains potentially vulnerable to indirect prompt injection carried inside migrated summary state.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Figure 3 (p. 6), and Section 5 (pp. 9–11, Tables 1–2 & Figure 4): "Evaluation across various scenarios shows that In-Mig achieves 92% similarity to centralized baselines, while preserving strict data locality... Table 1 and Fig. 4 report venue-wise latency: LLM inference averaged 5.1 s, memory update 1.1 s."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: In-Mig enables cross-institutional LLM reasoning via migrating JADE agents and sandboxed local Ollama runtimes, achieving 92% similarity to centralized baselines with 5.1 s inference and 1.1 s memory update latency per venue while keeping raw data local.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Multi-venue mobile-agent LLM prototype (JADE + Ollama) evaluated across 4 medical/legal venues in Comput. Mater. Contin. (2026)
Protected_Object: Venue-local raw medical/legal datasets and migrating agent summary memories
Composition_Evidence: Chains cryptographic venue admission and agent migration (B2), sandboxed local LLM inference over private institutional data (B3), and policy-enforced outbound summary redaction (B4) across 4 venues (Figure 3, p. 6; Table 1, p. 10).
Coding_Rationale: Artikel CMC (2026, 15 hlm.) yang mengimplementasikan agen bergerak JADE + Ollama terisolasi dengan metrik latensi per-venue (5,1 dtk inferensi + 1,1 dtk pembaruan memori) dan kesamaan kualitas 92% terhadap baseline terpusat.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: InfrastructureSentinel: Policy Enforced Guardrails for Secure MCP-driven Infrastructure Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Prompt injection, destructive command execution, privilege escalation, and tool poisoning across enterprise MCP-driven cloud/infrastructure management servers (Figure 1, p. 3).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: InfrastructureSentinel four-layer interception guardrail architecture (Input Validation Layer, Intent/Context Verification Layer, Policy Enforcement Layer, and Infrastructure Execution/Audit Layer; Figures 1–2, pp. 3–6).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Four Interception Layers between AI Agent, MCP Server, and Enterprise Infrastructure (Figures 1–2, pp. 3, 6)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Defense-in-depth interception of unauthorized or destructive MCP infrastructure commands with a False Positive Rate (FPR) under 10% and transparent audit trails (Table 1, p. 5).
Trust_Assumptions: All agent-to-infrastructure MCP tool calls traverse the four InfrastructureSentinel interception layers.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Experimental evaluation comparing attack detection across interception layers (Table 1, p. 5) demonstrates multi-layered blocking of malicious infrastructure commands while maintaining a False Positive Rate (FPR) under 10%.
Exposed_Security_Function: Four-layer policy-enforced guardrails for MCP-driven enterprise infrastructure management (InfrastructureSentinel)
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: False Positive Rate approaching 10% (p. 5) may still disrupt high-frequency automated DevOps/SRE workflows, and no cryptographic capability-token reduction is provided.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Figure 1 (p. 3), Table 1 (p. 5), and Figure 2 (p. 6): "InfrastructureSentinel: Policy Enforced Guardrails for Secure MCP-driven Infrastructure Management... Four Interception Layers (Figure 1)... Table 1: Experimental Results Comparing Attack Detection... maintaining a False Positive Rate (FPR) under 10%."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: InfrastructureSentinel enforces four interception guardrail layers across Agent-MCP-Infrastructure flows, blocking malicious infrastructure commands while keeping the False Positive Rate under 10%.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Enterprise MCP infrastructure guardrail prototype and attack-detection evaluation by Hewlett Packard Enterprise (7 pp.)
Protected_Object: MCP infrastructure management commands, cloud/server configurations, and execution audit logs
Composition_Evidence: Sequentially composes prompt/intent validation (B1), MCP tool-call policy interception (B3), and infrastructure command execution auditing (B4) across four interception points (Figures 1–2, pp. 3, 6).
Coding_Rationale: Studi Stream A dari Hewlett Packard Enterprise (7 hlm.) yang mengevaluasi 4 lapisan intersepsi InfrastructureSentinel pada Tabel 1 (hlm. 5) dengan FPR < 10%.
