Study_Title: Integrated Framework for Secure Communication among Multiple Agents using MCP and A2A
Threat_Attacker_Model: Message payload tampering, unauthorized inter-agent requests, stale message replay outside a 30-second window, and cascading task-chain failures across MCP-A2A multi-agent workflows (Section III-C, pp. 338–339 / PDF pp. 4–5).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Pre-shared symmetric secret key HMAC-SHA256 signature verification (expected_sig = HMAC_SHA256(secret_key, CONCAT(payload, timestamp))) combined with a 30-second UTC timestamp freshness check (|t_current - t_msg| <= 30 s) in Algorithm 1 (Section III-C, pp. 338–339 / PDF pp. 4–5). Contains NO PKI, NO asymmetric signed JSON tokens, and NO ephemeral session keying.
Enforcement_Point_Location: A2A Inter-Agent HTTP Endpoint & FastAPI MCP Server Tool Boundary (Figures 1–2, pp. 337–338 / PDF pp. 3–4)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Symmetric message integrity/authenticity under a static shared secret key and rejection of replays older than 30 seconds (Algorithm 1, p. 339 / PDF p. 5).
Trust_Assumptions: All four disaster-management agents (A1–A4) and the FastAPI MCP server share a single static pre-shared secret key in a trusted local environment and maintain synchronized UTC clocks.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluates a 4-agent disaster-management pipeline (A1 Disaster Analyzer -> A2 Impact Assessor -> A3 Resource Allocator -> A4 Logistics Deployer) running Qwen 2.5 7B via Ollama on an NVIDIA RTX 3050 (4 GB VRAM, 300 s HTTPX timeout) across 4 operational fault scenarios (Section V, pp. 340–341 / PDF pp. 6–7, Figures 3–6): Baseline (100% chain completion), Early-Chain Failure at A1 (0% completion), Mid-Chain Failure at A2 (25% completion), and High Context Load (~3,000 tokens, 100% completion). No adversarial cryptanalysis or ms cryptographic overhead is measured.
Exposed_Security_Function: Static pre-shared HMAC-SHA256 payload + UTC timestamp signature verification (30 s window, Algorithm 1) across A2A and MCP endpoints
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Uses a single static pre-shared secret key without per-agent PKI, asymmetric signatures, ephemeral session keys, or a seen-nonce cache (allowing replay within the 30 s window), and evaluates only operational fault/load scenarios (Baseline 100%, Early-Failure 0%, Mid-Failure 25%, High-Load 100%) rather than adversarial attacks.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Section III-C (pp. 338–339 / PDF pp. 4–5, Algorithm 1) & Section V (pp. 340–341 / PDF pp. 6–7, Figures 3–6): "Algorithm 1 Secure Message Verification Protocol: if |t_current - t_msg| > 30s then return Reject (Expired Timestamp); expected_sig <- HMAC_SHA256(secret_key, CONCAT(payload, timestamp))... Section V evaluates four operational scenarios: Scenario 1 Baseline (100% chain completion), Scenario 2 Early-Chain Failure (0%), Scenario 3 Mid-Chain Failure (25%), Scenario 4 High Context Load (100%)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: An integrated MCP and A2A multi-agent framework secures inter-agent communication using HMAC-SHA256 over payload and UTC timestamp with a 30-second freshness window (Algorithm 1), achieving 100% chain completion in baseline and high-context-load scenarios on Qwen 2.5 7B.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 4-agent disaster-management PoC (Qwen 2.5 7B on RTX 3050) using static pre-shared HMAC-SHA256 + 30s timestamp checks and tested on 4 operational fault/load scenarios
Protected_Object: A2A inter-agent JSON payloads, UTC timestamps, and FastAPI MCP tool requests
Composition_Evidence: Combines A2A sequential task handoffs signed with HMAC-SHA256 + 30s timestamp checks (B2) with synchronous FastAPI MCP tool invocations for disaster-response data retrieval (B3) across agents A1–A4 (Figures 1–2, pp. 337–338).
Coding_Rationale: KOREKSI AUDIT KRITIS pada baris pilot EXTRACTED (CLM-0020 / SLR-M-0178): draf v1.1 mengklaim adanya PKI, signed JSON tokens asimetris, ephemeral session keying, dan 100% completion di bawah kondisi adversarial. Audit PDF asli (hlm. 338–341) membuktikan protokol hanya memakai satu secret_key statis dengan HMAC-SHA256(secret_key, CONCAT(payload, timestamp)) + jendela 30 detik (Algorithm 1, hlm. 339) tanpa PKI/ephemeral keys, dan menguji 4 skenario kegagalan operasional (100%, 0%, 25%, 100%). Target_Boundary diselaraskan ke MULTI_BOUNDARY (B2;B3), Implementation_Maturity ke PROOF_OF_CONCEPT, dan Claim_Support_Status ke PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED (AD;UG).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Integrating agentic risk signalling in trusted research environments: Automating VEX with Agent2Agent protocols and model context protocol (MCP) in SACRO and TREvolution pipelines
Threat_Attacker_Model: Unverified software/AI vulnerabilities, tampered exploitability status, and non-reproducible agentic workflows inside high-assurance Trusted Research Environments (TREs) using A2A and MCP (pp. 1–4).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Automated generation, cryptographic signing, JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 validation (p. 9), and tamper-proof execution fingerprinting of machine-readable Vulnerability-Exploitability eXchange (VEX) and CSAF advisories integrated into A2A/MCP Trusted Research Environments (Figure 1, pp. 3–4; p. 13).
Enforcement_Point_Location: TRE Runtime Risk-Signalling Pipeline & Cryptographic VEX Attestation Verifier (Figure 1, pp. 3–4)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Cryptographically assured binding between each VEX exploitability document, container state, job execution fingerprint, and analytical lineage in TREs (pp. 4, 13).
Trust_Assumptions: TRE container runtime monitor and cryptographic signing keys are protected within the Accredited Trusted Research Environment.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Presents the automated VEX signing/validation methodology (Figure 1, pp. 3–4) and JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 compliance checks (p. 9), while qualitatively acknowledging computational and latency overhead from multi-layered runtime monitoring (Abstract, p. 1; p. 11).
Exposed_Security_Function: Cryptographically signed runtime VEX/CSAF risk signalling and execution fingerprinting for A2A/MCP Trusted Research Environments
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: explicitly acknowledges computational and latency overhead from multi-layered monitoring and scanner dependency (pp. 1, 11) without providing quantitative millisecond/throughput tables.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Figure 1 (pp. 3–4), Section 4 (p. 9), and Conclusion (p. 13): "This work provides both a proof-of-concept and a roadmap for refining security practices in sensitive computational environments... Every VEX document produced is verifiably linked to a specific job, container state, and analytical lineage, creating a robust and audit-ready security footprint."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Integrating cryptographically signed VEX/CSAF risk signalling and execution fingerprinting into A2A/MCP Trusted Research Environments links every vulnerability attestation to a specific job, container state, and analytical lineage.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Proof-of-concept architecture for automated signed VEX risk signalling in Trusted Research Environments (14 pp.)
Protected_Object: Machine-readable VEX/CSAF documents, TRE container states, and A2A/MCP analytical lineage logs
Composition_Evidence: Links runtime MCP tool and container execution monitoring (B3) with A2A risk signalling (B2) and cryptographically signed VEX/CSAF audit attestations (B4) inside Trusted Research Environments (Figure 1, pp. 3–4).
Coding_Rationale: Studi Stream M (Oxford, Cisco, Alan Turing Institute, Warwick, UWE, 14 hlm.) yang menyajikan PoC penandatanganan kriptografis dokumen VEX/CSAF di lingkungan TRE berbasis A2A/MCP; dikodekan PROOF_OF_CONCEPT dan PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED (AD;UG) karena overhead pemantauan baru dibahas secara kualitatif (hlm. 1, 11).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Invisible Prompts, Visible Threats: Malicious Font Injection in External Resources for Large Language Models
Threat_Attacker_Model: External resource publisher who modifies TrueType/OpenType font character-mapping tables (cmap / IdDelta code segments, Figure 1, p. 3) in external PDF/web documents retrieved via MCP or web search so human readers see benign text while LLM parsers extract malicious instructions.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (Malicious Font Injection attack manipulating font cmap IdDelta glyph-to-Unicode mappings in external documents ingested via MCP/RAG; Figures 1–2, p. 3).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Document Font Parser & MCP External Resource Ingestion Pipeline (Figures 1–2, p. 3)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Bypasses human visual inspection while coercing LLMs into Scenario 1 (Malicious Content Relay, up to 70.00% ASR) and Scenario 2 (Sensitive Data Leakage across 3 NISI privacy sensitivity tiers; pp. 4–14).
Trust_Assumptions: Victim LLM agent extracts raw Unicode codepoints from external PDF/web resources via MCP without OCR cross-verification against rendered glyphs.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across Scenario 1 (Malicious Content Relay) and Scenario 2 (Sensitive Data Leakage across Low/Medium/High NISI sensitivity tiers, Table 3, p. 14), achieving up to 70.00% attack success rate in content relay (Section 4.1, p. 6) while remaining visually indistinguishable to human reviewers.
Exposed_Security_Function: Malicious Font Injection (cmap IdDelta manipulation) vulnerability benchmark across MCP/web external resources
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Defeated if the ingestion pipeline normalizes documents via optical character recognition (OCR) or compares rendered glyph bitmaps against extracted Unicode text.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Figure 1–2 (p. 3), Section 4.1 (p. 6), and Section 6 (pp. 13–14, Table 3): "Illustration of malicious font creation through code segment modification (IdDelta)... Scenario 1: Malicious Content Relay (achieving higher success rates up to 70.00%)... Scenario 2: Sensitive Data Leakage categorized into three sensitivity levels based on NISI framework (Table 3)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Malicious Font Injection modifies font cmap IdDelta tables in external MCP/web documents so visually benign text decodes into hidden prompt injections, achieving up to 70.00% ASR in content relay and inducing multi-tier sensitive data leakage.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Controlled benchmark of font-table indirect prompt injection across MCP/web document ingestion (Scenario 1 & Scenario 2, 15 pp.)
Protected_Object: External PDF/web documents ingested via MCP, LLM context integrity, and NISI-classified sensitive user data
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates how tampering with font glyph-to-Unicode tables in external resources (B4) silently poisons MCP document extraction (B3) and hijacks LLM prompt reasoning and data exfiltration (B1/B3) (Figures 1–2, p. 3).
Coding_Rationale: Studi Stream A (USF, Rutgers, Liverpool, 15 hlm.) yang mendemonstrasikan serangan Malicious Font Injection (manipulasi cmap IdDelta) pada dokumen eksternal MCP dengan ASR hingga 70,00% pada Scenario 1 dan kebocoran data sensitif 3 tingkat NISI pada Tabel 3 (hlm. 14).
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: IPIGUARD: A Novel Tool Dependency Graph-Based Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) embedded in untrusted external tool outputs attempting to trigger unauthorized tool invocations or poison tool arguments during multi-step LLM agent execution (pp. 1023–1025 / PDF pp. 1–3).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: IPIGuard Tool Dependency Graph (TDG) execution-decoupling architecture constructing a pre-execution DAG of Deterministic, Pending, and Resolved tool nodes before reading untrusted data, combined with CQRS-inspired read-only Query Node Expansion (NE), Argument Estimation, and Fake Tool Invocation (FTI) (Figures 1–2, pp. 1024–1025 / PDF pp. 2–3). Non-cryptographic architectural defense.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Pre-Data TDG Planner & Monitored TDG Traversal Interceptor (Figure 2, p. 1025 / PDF p. 3)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Prevents untrusted tool outputs from dynamically introducing unscheduled side-effecting tool nodes, reducing average Attack Success Rate (ASR) to 0.69% on GPT-4o-mini across 4 attacks on AgentDojo (Table 1, p. 1030 / PDF p. 8).
Trust_Assumptions: Initial user prompt is benign and read-only Query Tools can be distinguished from state-changing Command Tools (CQRS assumption, p. 1026 / PDF p. 4).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: On AgentDojo (97 tasks, 629 security cases across Workspace, Slack, Travel, Banking) across 6 LLMs (Table 1, p. 1030 / PDF p. 8): on GPT-4o-mini across 4 attacks, IPIGuard achieves 0.69% average ASR (vs. 13.16% No Defense and 22.26% Spotlight), 58.77% Utility under Attack (UA), and 67.01% Benign Utility (Section 4.2.1 p. 1028; 69.07% in Table 3 ablation). Overhead on GPT-4o-mini (Table 2, p. 1030): 13.88 s mean completion time (vs. 7.13 s No Defense, ~1.95x) and 14,605 / 560 input/output tokens (vs. 6,165 / 179, ~2.37x input tokens).
Exposed_Security_Function: Pre-execution Tool Dependency Graph (TDG) construction, read-only Query Node Expansion (NE), and Fake Tool Invocation (FTI)
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Cannot completely block argument poisoning when the attacker's target tool overlaps with a legitimate tool already present in the planned TDG (residual 0.69% ASR, Section 6 Limitations, p. 1032 / PDF p. 10), and incurs ~2x latency (13.88 s vs. 7.13 s) and ~2.4x token overhead.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1023 / PDF p. 1), Section 3 (pp. 1025–1027 / PDF pp. 3–5, Figure 2), Section 4 (pp. 1028–1030 / PDF pp. 6–8, Tables 1–3), and Section 6 (p. 1032 / PDF p. 10): "IPIGUARD decouples action planning from external data ingestion by modeling the execution plan as a Tool Dependency Graph (TDG)... Table 1 (GPT-4o-mini average across 4 attacks): ASR 0.69%, UA 58.77%... Table 2: Time 13.88 s (vs 7.13 s), Tokens 14605 / 560 (vs 6165 / 179)."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: IPIGuard enforces a pre-planned Tool Dependency Graph (TDG) with read-only Query Node Expansion and Fake Tool Invocation on AgentDojo, reducing average ASR on GPT-4o-mini from 13.16% to 0.69% while preserving 58.77% Utility under Attack.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: EMNLP 2025 benchmark across 6 LLMs and 4 IPI attacks on AgentDojo (97 tasks, 629 security cases)
Protected_Object: LLM agent tool invocation sequence (TDG DAG) and tool-call argument resolution
Composition_Evidence: Decouples pre-data user-intent TDG planning (B1) from monitored tool traversal and Fake Tool Invocation (B3) while isolating untrusted external tool responses during argument estimation (B4) (Figure 2, p. 1025).
Coding_Rationale: Dekompisi klaim atomik (-A) dari baris pilot EXTRACTED (CLM-0009 / SLR-M-0181): menangkap mekanisme pertahanan utama TDG + NE + FTI dan efikasi penurunan ASR (0,69% rata-rata pada GPT-4o-mini di Tabel 1, hlm. 1030) dengan menyempurnakan Artifact_Protection_Lifetime menjadi EPHEMERAL_SESSION.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: IPIGUARD: A Novel Tool Dependency Graph-Based Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Tool-overlap argument poisoning (where the attacker's target tool coincides with a legitimate planned TDG node) and runtime token/latency overhead across 6 LLMs on AgentDojo (Tables 1–2, p. 1030; Limitations, p. 1032).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: IPIGuard TDG traversal, Argument Estimation, and Fake Tool Invocation (FTI) benchmarked for latency, token cost, and ablation sensitivity across 6 LLMs (Tables 1–3, pp. 1029–1031 / PDF pp. 7–9).
Enforcement_Point_Location: TDG Traversal Engine & Argument Estimation Module (pp. 1026–1030)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Quantifies the exact latency/token cost (13.88 s vs. 7.13 s; 14,605/560 vs. 6,165/179 tokens) and residual tool-overlap vulnerability boundary of TDG-based IPI defenses (Tables 2–3, p. 1030; p. 1032).
Trust_Assumptions: Evaluated on AgentDojo benchmark suites (Workspace, Slack, Travel, Banking) across 6 LLM backbones.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Table 2 (p. 1030 / PDF p. 8) reports GPT-4o-mini mean task latency of 13.88 s (vs. 7.13 s No Defense, 1.95x) and 14,605 input / 560 output tokens (vs. 6,165 / 179 No Defense, 2.37x input / 3.13x output); Table 3 ablation shows removing FTI drops Benign Utility from 69.07% to 55.67% and removing NE drops BU to 62.89%.
Exposed_Security_Function: AgentDojo latency/token overhead benchmark and NE/FTI component ablation analysis for IPIGuard
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: ~2x latency and ~2.4x input token overhead from separate planning/argument-estimation LLM calls, plus residual vulnerability when injected instructions hijack arguments of an already-scheduled tool node (p. 1032).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Section 4.3 (p. 1030 / PDF p. 8, Tables 2–3) & Section 6 (p. 1032 / PDF p. 10): "Table 2: No Defense 7.13s (6165 / 179 tokens) vs. IPIGuard 13.88s (14605 / 560 tokens)... Table 3 Ablation: IPIGuard BU 69.07%, w/o FTI 55.67%, w/o NE 62.89%... Limitations: when the attacker's target tool overlaps with the tools required for the user's normal task, argument manipulation may still occur."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: IPIGuard incurs 13.88 s mean task latency (vs. 7.13 s baseline) and 14,605/560 input/output tokens (vs. 6,165/179 baseline) on AgentDojo, while remaining vulnerable to argument poisoning when malicious and benign tool sets overlap.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: RQ3 performance overhead (Table 2), ablation (Table 3), and residual tool-overlap limitation analysis on AgentDojo
Protected_Object: TDG node argument estimation and multi-turn LLM token/latency budget
Composition_Evidence: Ablation in Table 3 (p. 1030) isolates how Fake Tool Invocation (FTI) and Query Node Expansion (NE) compose at the tool execution boundary (B3) to preserve benign utility (69.07% vs. 55.67% w/o FTI).
Coding_Rationale: Dekompisi klaim atomik (-B) untuk SLR-M-0181: memisahkan kuantifikasi overhead latensi/token (Tabel 2), ablasi komponen NE/FTI (Tabel 3), dan batasan residu tool-overlap argument poisoning (hlm. 1032) untuk menjawab RQ3 secara presisi.
Required_Additional_Evidence: NONE (Teks lengkap PDF ter-pin telah diaudit dan diekstraksi lengkap 38 kolom oleh REVIEWER_2).

Study_Title: Lineage: A UMA2.0 Protocol Extension for Multi-Hop LLM Agent Delegation
Threat_Attacker_Model: Multi-hop delegation privilege escalation, lineage spoofing, confused-deputy sub-agent tool access, and in-process token theft across autonomous LLM agent chains (>90% ASR against unprotected multi-hop baselines, p. 3).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Lineage UMA 2.0 protocol extension introducing a 7-field cryptographic Delegation Lineage Claim inside Requesting Party Tokens (RPTs), per-agent RFC 9449 DPoP proof-of-possession keys, and strict monotonic scope attenuation across multi-hop LLM agent delegation chains (Figure 1 & Tables 1–2, p. 5; Table 16, p. 17).
Enforcement_Point_Location: UMA 2.0 Authorization Server & Resource Server PEP on Multi-Hop Agent Boundaries (Figure 1, p. 5)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Protocol-layer deterministic blocking of multi-hop scope escalation, lineage tampering, and token replay independent of LLM model behavior (pp. 1, 5–17).
Trust_Assumptions: UMA 2.0 Authorization Server and Resource Server PEPs are trusted, and each agent holds an uncompromised per-agent DPoP private key.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Blocks 100% of multi-hop scope escalation, lineage forgery, and token replay attempts at the protocol layer independently of LLM behavior, while keeping per-request latency overhead negligible relative to the baseline OAuth 2.0 / UMA 2.0 stack (Abstract, p. 1; Sections V–VI, pp. 12–17; Table 16, p. 17).
Exposed_Security_Function: UMA 2.0 multi-hop Delegation Lineage extension (7-field lineage claim), monotonic scope attenuation, and per-agent DPoP binding
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Enforces structural scope and lineage attenuation at the UMA 2.0 protocol layer, but cannot prevent a sub-agent from misusing a legitimate narrow scope when manipulated by semantic prompt injection within that scope.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Section IV (p. 5, Figure 1 & Tables 1–2), and Section VI (p. 17, Table 16): "the protocol layer blocked it independently of model behavior, which is precisely the property a deployment operator needs to rely on. Per-request overhead remained negligible relative to the UMA 2.0 baseline... Table 1 defines its seven fields... Table 16 maps system requirements R1–R6 to the empirical evidence."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Lineage extends UMA 2.0 with a 7-field cryptographic delegation lineage claim and per-agent DPoP proof-of-possession keys, deterministically blocking multi-hop privilege escalation and token replay at the protocol layer with negligible overhead over baseline UMA 2.0.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Protocol extension specification, requirement validation (R1–R6, Table 16), and latency/security benchmarks across multi-hop LLM agent chains (18 pp.)
Protected_Object: UMA 2.0 Requesting Party Tokens (RPTs), 7-field delegation lineage claims, per-agent DPoP keys, and resource server APIs
Composition_Evidence: Cryptographically chains requesting-party consent (B1) through multi-hop sub-agent UMA ticket/RPT exchanges with DPoP binding (B2) to resource-server PEP enforcement (B3) and full lineage auditability (B4) (Figure 1 & Tables 1–2, p. 5; Table 16, p. 17).
Coding_Rationale: Studi M_AND_A (18 hlm.) yang sangat komprehensif: memperluas standar OAuth 2.0 / UMA 2.0 dengan 7-field Delegation Lineage dan DPoP per-agen serta memvalidasi persyaratan R1–R6 secara kuantitatif (Tabel 16, hlm. 17).

Enforcement_Point_Location: MCP-Secure Runtime Access Control Proxy between LLM Agent and MCP Servers (Figures 1–2, pp. 4–5)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Monotonic session-level privilege enforcement and least-privilege tool execution gating across multi-step MCP sessions (Table 1, p. 6; p. 9).
Trust_Assumptions: MCP-Secure proxy mediates all client-to-server MCP JSON-RPC calls and declarative tool privilege manifests are accurately specified.

Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Section VII (p. 9) notes reliance on accurate manual/static privilege declarations for each MCP tool and inability to inspect covert semantic exfiltration within an allowed privilege state.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1), Figures 1–2 (pp. 4–5), Section VI (p. 6, Table 1), and Section VII (p. 9): "MCP-Secure: A Runtime Access Control Layer for Privilege-Aware LLM Agent Tooling... Fig. 1 illustrates the session-level security state transition diagram... Table 1 shows that MCP-Secure produces clear, monotonic enforcement without modifying underlying agents or MCP servers."

Study_Title: MCPTox: A Benchmark for Tool Poisoning Attack on Real-World MCP Servers
Threat_Attacker_Model: Tool Poisoning Attacks (TPA) where malicious instructions are embedded directly inside the metadata descriptions of legitimate-looking tools hosted on real-world MCP servers (Figures 1–2, pp. 1–2).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NONE (MCPTox benchmark comprising 45+ real-world MCP servers, 353 tools, and 1,312 malicious test cases across 3 attack paradigms evaluated across 20 prominent LLM agents; Figures 1–2, pp. 1–2).
Enforcement_Point_Location: MCP Tool Metadata Ingestion & LLM Agent Planning Layer (Figure 2, p. 2)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Quantifies severe vulnerability of 20 LLM agents to metadata-level Tool Poisoning Attacks (up to 72.8% ASR on o1-mini; >60% on GPT-4o) and near-complete failure of existing safety alignment (<3% refusal rate; Abstract, p. 1).
Trust_Assumptions: LLM agent connects to external MCP servers and ingests their JSON tool descriptions into the system/planning prompt.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across 20 LLM agents on 1,312 test cases over 45+ real-world MCP servers: achieves up to 72.8% ASR (and >60% ASR on flagship models like GPT-4o), while more capable models often exhibit higher vulnerability due to superior instruction following, and existing safety alignment yields a refusal rate below 3% (Abstract & Section 1, pp. 1–2).
Exposed_Security_Function: MCPTox real-world MCP Tool Poisoning Attack (TPA) benchmark across 45+ servers and 20 LLM agents
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Diagnostic benchmark paper demonstrating that model-level safety alignment (<3% refusal) and static scanners fail against implicit tool-description poisoning, motivating architectural separation of tool metadata from control instructions.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract & Section 1 (pp. 1–2, Figures 1–2): "MCPTox comprises over 45 real-world MCP servers... evaluating 20 prominent LLM agents... achieving an attack success rate of 72.8% [and >60% on models such as GPT-4o], while the refusal rate is less than 3%, demonstrating that existing safety alignment is ineffective against TPA."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: On the MCPTox benchmark (45+ real-world MCP servers), Tool Poisoning Attacks achieve up to 72.8% ASR across 20 LLM agents while model safety alignment yields a refusal rate below 3%.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Large-scale empirical TPA benchmark across 45+ real-world MCP servers and 20 LLM agents (USTC & Beihang Univ., 9 pp.)
Protected_Object: MCP server tool metadata descriptions, LLM planning context, and local host files/credentials
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates how poisoned tool descriptions ingested during MCP server discovery (B2) hijack the agent into invoking privileged prerequisite tools (e.g., reading sensitive files before file operations at B3) (Figure 2, p. 2).
Coding_Rationale: Studi benchmark empiris fundamental (MCPTox, 9 hlm.) yang menguji 20 agen LLM pada >45 server MCP dunia nyata dan membuktikan ASR hingga 72,8% serta tingkat penolakan (refusal rate) <3%.

Study_Title: Model Context Protocol: A Comprehensive Analysis for AI-Assisted Database Query Generation in Multi-Dataset Research Platforms
Threat_Attacker_Model: Malicious SQL injection, unauthorized row-level PII extraction, and destructive non-aggregate queries generated by LLM front-ends over sensitive research databases (pp. 1–3).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Controlled MCP database querying architecture enforcing deterministic SQL AST validation (restricting execution strictly to aggregate-only SELECT queries via pre-approved MCP tools for schema exploration, table inspection, and aggregate execution) combined with 100% tool-invocation audit logging (Figure 1, p. 2; Table I, p. 3; pp. 4–5).
Enforcement_Point_Location: MCP Database Server Query Validator & Audit Logger (Figure 1, p. 2; pp. 3–5)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: 100% enforcement of aggregate-only SQL queries, 100% prevention of unauthorized row-level access, 100% blocking of malicious SQL injection attempts, and 100% tool-invocation audit coverage (Abstract, p. 1; Section IV, pp. 4–5).
Trust_Assumptions: Database access is strictly mediated through the MCP server's three restricted tools (schema exploration, table inspection, aggregate query) and direct raw SQL write endpoints are disabled.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Evaluated across AI-generated aggregate SQL workloads and adversarial SQLi/unauthorized-access test cases (Table I, p. 3; Section IV, pp. 4–5): achieves 100% query restriction compliance, 100% prevention of unauthorized access and SQL injection, 100% audit log coverage, and low end-to-end query execution latency.
Exposed_Security_Function: Aggregate-only SQL query enforcement and 100% invocation audit logging on MCP database servers
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Restricting the MCP server to aggregate-only queries blocks direct row dumps, but remains potentially vulnerable to differencing/inference attacks across repeated narrow aggregate queries (e.g., COUNT/SUM with tight WHERE predicates) and lacks cryptographic differential privacy.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: [PARAFRASA] Abstract (p. 1) & Section IV (pp. 3–5, Table I): "100% enforcement of aggregate only queries, 100% prevention of unauthorised access, and 100% blocking of malicious SQL... system yielded 100% query restriction compliance... 100% tool invocation coverage in the audit logging mechanism."
Claim_Text_As_Reported: An MCP-based database querying framework enforces aggregate-only SQL execution and mandatory audit logging, achieving 100% query restriction compliance, 100% prevention of unauthorized access and SQL injection, and 100% audit coverage.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Controlled evaluation of MCP-mediated aggregate SQL querying over sensitive research datasets (6 pp.)
Protected_Object: Sensitive research database records, MCP SQL query tools, and invocation audit logs
Composition_Evidence: Couples pre-execution SQL query restriction and aggregate-only validation at the MCP tool boundary (B3) with mandatory 100% tool-invocation audit logging over sensitive research datasets (B4) (Figure 1, p. 2; pp. 4–5).
Coding_Rationale: Studi Stream A (6 hlm.) yang mengevaluasi pembatasan kueri SQL hanya-agregat melalui server MCP dengan hasil 100% kepatuhan restriksi kueri, 100% pemblokiran SQLi/akses tidak sah, dan 100% cakupan log audit (hlm. 1, 4–5).
